title: New 2027 BMW 3 Series Previewed With 443-HP Straight-Six

body_markdown:
BMW dusted off the i3 name[earlier in 2026](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-bmw-i3-3-series-specs-pictures-performance/) to use it on the electric version of the new 3 Series, but the sedan isn’t going EV-only. The gasoline-powered 2027 BMW 3 Series is coming soon, and the range will include four- and six-cylinder-powered variants.


Photos of a fully camouflaged pre-production car testing on BMW’s Miramas, France, test track confirm that the next 3 Series will look a lot like the i3 when viewed from the outside. We expect that the camouflage hides a handful of powertrain-specific styling cues, such as air intakes, but it looks like the easiest way to tell the 3 Series and the i3 apart will be to look for the exhaust outlets poking out of the rear bumper. Both sedans wear a new design language inspired by[the Neue Klasse concept](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/neue-klasse-concept-is-another-divisive-design-from-bmw/) introduced in 2023.


BMW tells us that the new 3 Series rides on a longer wheelbase than[the outgoing model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2019-bmw-3-series-first-drive/) , with wider front and rear tracks and a near-50/50 front-rear weight distribution. There’s a great deal of technology packed into the 3 as well, including steering updates and newly developed dampers. BMW claims that these updates give the new 3 noticeably more agile handling than its predecessor.

Details about the model range are beginning to trickle out. The M3[will return](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/confirmed-next-gen-bmw-m3-will-offer-both-all-electric-and-gas-power/) , and while it hasn’t been unveiled yet, we know that it will be available with either a turbocharged straight-six or an electric drivetrain. The next model down in the hierarchy (and the only member of the core range offered with six cylinders) will be the M350 xDrive. The engine in question is a 3.0-liter, twin-turbocharged straight-six rated at 443 horsepower and 428 pound-feet of torque. That’s enough for a 4.1-second sprint to 60 mph.


An eight-speed automatic transmission, the xDrive all-wheel-drive system, and a 48-volt mild-hybrid system will come standard. It doesn’t sound like a manual will be available, but drivers will be able to bypass the xDrive system and send 100% of the engine’s power to the rear wheels thanks to a new driving mode called Drift Moment. The M350 will further stand out from other 3 Series models with variable sport steering, an adaptive M suspension system, and an M Sport differential.


Interestingly, the Drift Moment feature won’t be available at launch. It will be added in 2027 via an over-the-air software update.


The M350 will replace the M340i as the track-inspired, M Performance variant of the core 3 Series—remember that BMW[is ditching](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bmw-axes-the-i-from-combustion-cars/) the “i” from its gasoline-burning cars because the letter now denotes EVs. The brand hasn’t detailed the other 3 Series variants yet, but it confirmed that volume-oriented, four-cylinder-powered trims positioned below the M350 are coming as well.


More details about the 2027 BMW 3 Series will emerge in the coming months, and we’ll see it in the metal by the end of 2026.
